title: EMS Providers Gather in Johnson City This Week for Key Training at Northeast TN EMS Conference - NewsBreak
text:
1 hours ago David Blevins, program Director at Roane State Community College presents a lecture. Photo by courtesy of Northeast Tennessee Emergency Medical & Rescue Conference Johnson City, Tenn. — Emergency medical and rescue professionals from Tennessee, North Carolina, and Virginia will unite Thursday and Friday at the Holiday Inn–Johnson City for the Northeast Tennessee Emergency Medical & Rescue Conference, offering vital instruction, case studies and networking aimed at strengthening regional response capacity.
What It Is and Why It Matters The Northeast Tennessee Emergency Medical & Rescue Conference , hosted by Washington County‑Johnson City EMS, brings together EMS and rescue workers for two days of continuing education, emerging trends, and shared experiences. The conference is approved for contact hours by the State Offices of Emergency Medical Services in Tennessee, North Carolina, and Virginia—making it a key event for providers needing license renewal. wcjcems.org
When & Where Dates: Thursday and Friday of this week — September 11–12. wcjcems.org Location: Holiday Inn, Johnson City, Tennessee. AllEvents Registration begins at 6:30 a.m. both mornings. wcjcems.org Key Topics & Speakers Over the two days, sessions will cover topics ranging from neuro emergencies, pediatric stroke, point‑of‑care ultrasound in pre‑hospital settings , to hazardous materials response, and PTSD among first responders. wcjcems.org
Noteworthy speakers include:
Dr. David Carle — “Point of Care Ultrasound in Pre‑Hospital Settings” wcjcems.org Melisa Taylor — “PTSD” wcjcems.org Katie Hall — covering both “Pediatric Stroke” and “Stroke Considerations” wcjcems.org Who Should Attend The conference is designed for EMS and rescue professionals, first responders, instructors, and agency decision‑makers. With its multistate approval for continuing education, it’s especially relevant for those needing license renewal or wishing to stay abreast of best practices in disaster response, emergency medicine, and post‑incident care. wcjcems.org
Practical Details Contact hours are awarded by the Tennessee, North Carolina, and Virginia EMS offices. wcjcems.org Vendor booths will be part of the event, providing opportunities to explore new equipment and resources. wcjcems.org Lunch is included for those registered in advance. wcjcems.org
